messages:
maria: heads-up — SCIM provisioning to Okta started failing after last night's KMS rotation. lots of 400/403s and some "decryption failed" errors in the provisioner logs. anyone seen this pattern?
aj: can you paste the exact error log line? is it KMS decrypt or SAML assertion decrypt?
maria: paste from the provisioner: ```
2026-03-19T23:12:04Z ERROR scim-sync service_account=svc-scim-01 msg="failed to decrypt assertion" err="kms.Decrypt: invalid encryption context" code=400
2026-03-19T23:12:04Z WARN  scim-sync user=acct-123 action=provision target=okta status=failed
```
maria: we rotated the key alias redwood/idp-enc last night as part of scheduled rotation. SCIM uses the same service principal that reads the KMS key.
devon: very likely the new key version doesn't have the old encryption context or the service account IAM binding. quick check: does the KMS key policy include the SCIM service account and the SAML proxy identity?
irina: also check Okta/IdP SAML settings — if assertions are encrypted with a public key tied to the previous key version, the sp may not be able to decrypt after key switch. but your error looks like KMS-level decrypt.
aj: run a local decrypt test as the svc principal. For GCP KMS: ```gcloud kms keys versions decrypt --key=projects/xxx/locations/global/keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/idp-enc --ciphertext-file=cipher.bin --plaintext-file=out.txt --location=global``` replace with your key path. If it errors with invalid encryption context, the context used at encrypt time differs.
maria: ok will run that. fyi we also noticed audit events for RBAC changes (granting svc-scim permission) are not showing up in the audit log stream. might be related — I submitted a support ticket to cloud-ops.
devon: audit gap could be a separate IAM propagation delay or a logging sink misconfig. check the cloud audit log filter and sink permissions. if the service account was created+granted in same window as key rotation, propagation could be partial.
irina: short mitigation: roll the key alias back to the previous CryptoKeyVersion that still has the old encryption context and IAM bindings, then force a resync. not ideal long-term but gets provisioning back quickly.
security-bot: INCIDENT created: INC-2026-1036 (sso-provisioning-kms-decrypt). severity: P2. assigned: eng-security + infra-oncall.
oncall-bot: Pager duty alert triggered for infra-oncall (devon).
aj: if you need a hotfix without touching keys, you can temporarily accept unencrypted assertions on the SP side (if idp supports) for a short window, but only if network/tenant risk is low. prefer key rollback first.
maria: rolled alias back to previous version at 23:44, requeued pending SCIM jobs. first run shows some successes but still a handful of "invalid encryption context" entries.
devon: those lingering failures likely correspond to tokens/encrypted blobs created after the rotation before rollback. try rotating the tokens by re-encrypting cached artifacts or force-expiring the affected sessions.
irina: added commands to verify KMS IAM: ```
# list bindings
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy idp-enc --location=global --keyring=kr
# check cryptoKeyVersion state
gcloud kms keys versions list --key=idp-enc --location=global --keyring=kr
```
maria: did that — found that svc-scim was missing on the new CryptoKeyVersion IAM binding. we added it back and reprocessed queue. provisioning green now for ~95% tenants.
aj: great — follow-up: add a pre-rotation checklist step to verify that future key versions inherit IAM bindings and that any KMS encryption context used by downstream services is recorded in the rotation playbook.
devon: also create a short-runbook for ops: keys -> verify bindings -> run decrypt smoke -> requeue scim -> monitor audit logs. link to runbook PR when ready.
security-bot: postmortem request filed: PM-2026-88, include root cause (missing binding on new key version) and remediation (rotation checklist + runbook + alert for failed decrypt-rate > 1% over 5m).
maria: thanks all. leaving notes in the ticket and will open a doc for the runbook. :thumbsup:
aj: can someone add me as reviewer on the runbook? I'll add the audit log checks.
maria: will do. closing this thread once postmortem doc is in draft.
